paper_sections.title: Reduced Functional Connectivity within the Mesocorticolimbic System in Substance Use Disorders: An fMRI Study of Puerto Rican Young Adults

description.value: The study examined resting-state functional connectivity within the mesocorticolimbic system in Puerto Rican young adults with and without a substance use disorder, and explored relationships among connectivity, impulsivity, SUD, and scan site.

design.value: Cross-sectional, two-site resting-state fMRI study comparing young adults with SUD (SUD+) and without SUD (SUD−), with group comparisons, site moderation, partial correlation, and path analysis.

name.value: large, epidemiological study of Puerto Ricans in the South Bronx, New York and San Juan, Puerto Rico
World Health Organization Composite International Diagnostic Interview Version (CIDI)

description.value: Diagnostic interviews, including assessments of SUD and comorbid psychiatric conditions, using the English or Spanish schedules of the WHO CIDI Tobacco, Alcohol Use and Illegal SU modules.

task_description.value: Participants were instructed to remain still with their eyes closed and to let their minds wander freely. Two 5-min resting-state scans were obtained for each participant.

instructions.value: Remain still with eyes closed and let their minds wander freely.

instrument.value: GE MR750 3.0 Tesla whole body scanner

description.value: Two 5-min resting-state scans were obtained for each participant. Axial echoplanar images were obtained to provide whole-brain coverage.

instrument.value: GE MR750 3.0 Tesla whole body scanner

description.value: A high-resolution anatomical image was acquired for coregistration with axial echoplanar images.

The functional images were slice time and motion corrected, coregistered with a high-resolution anatomical scan, normalized into MNI space, resampled at 2 mm3, and smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of 6 mm3 FWHM. Connectivity preprocessing followed component-based noise correction.

steps.value: coregistration with a high-resolution anatomical scan
normalization into Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space
smoothing with a Gaussian kernel of 6 mm3 full width at half maximum

model_settings.value: Group as the single factor with two levels (SUD+ and SUD−), with comorbid disorders as a covariate dummy coded 1 or 0; motion parameters were included as nuisance regressors at the subject- and group-level.
The dependent variable was MCLS connectivity, and the independent variables were Group, Site, and a Group by Site interaction term.
Two linear regression models and bias corrected bootstrapping were used to examine associations between impulsivity, MCLS connectivity, and SUD.

name.value: Main effect of site on MCLS connectivity

definition.value: Neither a main effect of site ... was significant (p > 0.3).

name.value: Group by Site interaction on MCLS connectivity

definition.value: Neither the group (SUD+ vs. SUD−) by site interaction was significant (p > 0.3).

interpretations.value: Whether the relationship between SUD and altered MCLS connectivity differed at the two sites

name.value: Partial correlation between left NAcc–left OFC connectivity and impulsivity

roi_definition.value: region in which MCLS connectivity differed between SUD+ and SUD− participants

definition.value: Partial correlations between MCLS connectivity and impulsivity, while controlling for site and group; impulsivity correlated inversely with the connection strength between the left NAcc and the left OFC.

interpretations.value: The connection strength between the left NAcc and the OFC correlated with impulsivity.

name.value: Path analysis: impulsivity associated with low MCLS connectivity

definition.value: In the first linear regression model, impulsivity was significantly associated with low MCLS connectivity (left NAcc − left OFC connection strength; beta = −0.006, t = −2.13, p = 0.043).

reason_first_class_type_not_used.value: Path analysis is not one of the five named first-class method families.

interpretations.value: Impulsivity may contribute to the development of SUD through its effects on the MCLS.

name.value: Path analysis: MCLS connectivity predicting SUD while controlling for impulsivity

definition.value: In the second linear regression model, while controlling for impulsivity, MCLS connectivity was a significant predictor of SUD (−14.37, z = −2.27, p = 0.024, Wald = 5.13).

reason_first_class_type_not_used.value: Path analysis is not one of the five named first-class method families.

interpretations.value: MCLS connectivity was a significant predictor of SUD.

name.value: Path analysis: indirect effect of impulsivity on SUD mediated by MCLS connectivity

definition.value: Bias corrected bootstrapping confirmed the significance of the indirect effect of impulsivity on SUD as mediated by MCLS connectivity (coefficient = 0.081; 95% CI = 0.013–0.522).

mediation_path.value: indirect effect of impulsivity on SUD as mediated by MCLS connectivity

interpretations.value: Support for a potential mechanism relating impulsivity, MCLS connectivity, and SUD.
